rows: Record Q2: first quarter ever above $300M in single-quarter sales (~$326M, +112%).
Third full quarter inside PepsiCo distribution; integration exceeded all internal expectations and budgets.
Biggest expected gain from Pepsi was convenience & gas distribution, which delivered the largest ACV gains.
Foodservice an unexpected surprise at 11% of Pepsi revenue; seen as future scale/growth lever.
Gross margin up >1,000 bps to 48.8%, driven by lower packaging/raw-material cost, less waste/scrap, ~100 bps freight efficiency.
G&A elevated to 10% of sales primarily on a $7.9M securities class action settlement accrual; underlying G&A near historical rates.
Management declines to issue formal forward guidance; framed results as a beat vs internal budgets.
Q3 P&L classification shift: '100 days of summer' incentives move spend from S&M into promotional allowances (contra-revenue), reducing reported top-line without affecting EBITDA/net income.
Distributor inventory build was not a key Q2 driver (<$5M); DIO consistent quarter-over-quarter at a preferred level.
International expansion early-stage: 2023 a planning year; blueprint in a handful of countries in 2024, broader expansion 2025-2026.
Innovation launches planned for 2024 and beyond; no specifics disclosed.
Club channel expansion incremental with no observed cannibalization; draws somewhat older incremental consumers.
Cold placements and secondary displays critical to capturing impulse purchases and building loyalty; Celsius-branded coolers a major push.
Capacity expanding from a six-orbit to eight-orbit co-packer model in H2; ~17 co-packers; 95%+ shipping rate.
Material weakness remediation progressing well; full clearance only after year-end testing. SEC review ongoing, no new updates.
Buyers signaling 2024 resets may cut juice/CST space to give more shelf space to energy.
Management tone highly confident and upbeat throughout.
Q2 exit rate & foodservice channel sizing
Asked about Q2 exit rate / quarter-to-date trends, and the size of Pepsi revenue plus how to think about the foodservice channel as the school year starts.

Declined forward guidance but said the company performed extremely well. Foodservice = 11% of Pepsi revenue (includes colleges, which were down for the summer); Celsius University launched (170 students) and back-to-campus is a Q3 opportunity. Pepsi revenue was ~56.7% of total revenue.
Were they surprised by the level of distribution via Pepsi and which channels surprised; how much of shelf-space gain came from other energy brands vs incremental coolers.

Pepsi relationship exceeded all expectations; convenience & gas the biggest expected gain and largest ACV driver; foodservice an unexpected surprise. ~14.6 US spacings (up sizably from start of year); mix of Pepsi energy coolers and dedicated Celsius coolers; unclear if space taken from other brands but gained incrementally.

Updated thoughts on international rollout (markets, share opportunity, contribution); and drivers of gross margin upside vs prior mid-40% expectation, plus whether the mid-to-high 40s H2 outlook is conservatism.

Competitor proxy of 35-40% international revenue mix as 'size of the prize'; focus on energy-familiar countries; launches targeted early 2024; 3-5 year opportunity. Margin: prior mid-40s target refined to low end of mid-40s in H1, high end in H2; ~100 bps freight help (variable, not locked); slotting and contra-revenue pressure in H2 - hence pointing to high-end of mid-40s.
Summer stocking, Q3 growth & production capacity

How much Q2 benefited from summer stocking vs sell-through, whether channel inventory was elevated, how to think about Q3 growth/moderation; and whether production capacity is sufficient given club stockouts.

DIO consistent QoQ with <$5M benefit, expected to hold into Q3. Q2 was solid all-around with slight velocity expansion and marketing pushes (MLS, Jake Paul fight, 100 days of summer); scan data suggests trends maintained. Capacity: 95%+ shipping, ~17 co-packers, moving to eight-orbit model in H2 to ensure shelf stocking.
Secondary placements / branded coolers & Q3 promotional spend

How big a push behind secondary placements / branded fridges and how much distribution upside they represent; can the greater 100-days-of-summer promo spend be quantified and would a promo price cut show in scanner data.

Secondary displays and especially cold placements critical to capturing impulse purchases; Celsius coolers a big push (Cosmic Vibe at Circle K, 7-Eleven support). Biggest forward opportunity is more SKUs in cold placements. Declined to fully quantify promo spend - some contra-revenue incentives won't appear in scan data; promotional activity ~20% of gross sales, up a bit in Q3.
Clarification on distributor inventory - whether prior-quarter channel fill (~$20-25M) reverses or settles at a new normal; and drivers of non-measured channel strength (Costco, Sam's, BJ's, Amazon).

Q2 DIO impact <$5M, de minimis; DIO very consistent QoQ; inventories low in Q4 now at preferred level, expected to continue into Q3; Q4 a partner decision. Non-measured channel strength from Vibe pack rollout (two packs in Costco), promotional activity, and Sam's Club rollout.
How many club channel consumers are incremental/new to the brand; are they like traditional coffee/tea consumers given Celsius's differentiated positioning.

Club expansion incremental with no observed cannibalization; 50-50 male/female, 18-to-45-plus demographic means club draws an incremental, somewhat older consumer; cited sampling and unit-growth leadership in liquid refrigerated beverages.
Legal settlement classification & sales & marketing outlook
Is 100% of the legal settlement in G&A; and more color on S&M - whether it came in lower than expected and what to expect in H2 given contra-revenue promotion.

Confirmed 100% of settlement in G&A. S&M ran 19-20% vs a closer-to-22% expectation, reflecting sales beat plus system leverage and below-budget headcount. H2 S&M to move toward ~22% historical rate, some bucketed into contra-revenue; advertising slightly ahead of historical rates, savings in storage/warehousing.
Given headcount expansion seems not very aggressive, where will the additions go and what is the goal.
Applying additional resources as it scales; H2 headcount planned across operations, marketing, and sales; reiterated 170 Celsius University students heading to campuses.
